newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa prays for Albanians.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa prays for Albanians.

text.p: Mother Teresa said on Friday that she was praying for the people of Albania, where a chaotic revolt was sweeping her parents' country.
"I'm praying for them," the Nobel Peace Prize winner told a news conference when asked to comment on the troubles in Albania.
Tanks moved onto the streets of Tirana late on Thursday night in an attempt to stem virtual anarchy gripping the country.
Mother Teresa was born Agnes Goinxha Bejaxhiu to Albanian parents in Skopje, in what was then Serbia, on August 27, 1910.
She later became a Loretto nun and established her Missionaries of Charity religious order in the eastern Indian city of Calcutta in 1948.
On Thursday nuns from the order elected Sister Nirmala, a Hindu convert to Roman Catholicism, to succeed the 86-year-old Mother Teresa at the head of the missionary.
Sister Nirmala, 63, appeared at the news conference beside Mother Teresa in the courtyard of Mother House, the order's headquarters in India's most densely populated city.
